item.title: Version 1.1.0
item.description:
• A new Apps pane shows what each app is using, with its helper processes added in, and the busiest apps appear in the menu bar panel.

• Charts go back 3 minutes, 1 hour or 24 hours, show the time, and show readings as you hover. History is kept between launches.

• New GPU, Disk and Network panes, plus thermal state, CPU and GPU temperatures and fan speeds.

• A desktop widget, and Shortcuts actions for CPU, memory, GPU, power and the busiest apps.

• The CPU meter can show every core, one bar for each type of core, or just the total.

• Charts no longer draw a line across times Usage Finder wasn't measuring.

item.title: Version 1.0.5
item.description:
Each menu bar meter (CPU, memory and power) is now its own item. Choose which ones to show in Settings → Menu Bar, and hold Command to drag them into any order.

With every meter turned off, Usage Finder shows its icon and does no background work.

item.title: Version 1.0.4
item.description:
Show power use in the menu bar as a level meter with the wattage beside it.

Settings has a fresh glass look, keeps one size for every tab, and picks the meter colour with a slider.

The menu bar panel's bars now match your meter colour.

item.title: Version 1.0.3
item.description: Choose Light Green for the menu bar meters, alongside Blue and Black & White.

item.title: Version 1.0.2
item.description:
New welcome window that explains the menu bar meters: which bars are Efficiency and Performance cores, memory and swap, and what the percentages mean. Open it again from Help → Welcome to Usage Finder.

Smoother power history when power comes from the battery's power monitor.

Settings → General now shows which edition you're running.

item.title: Version 1.0.1
item.description:
First public release of Usage Finder.

Live CPU, memory, swap and power meters in the menu bar, with history charts in the main window.

Updates now install automatically from Settings → General.
